read: turns [00:02] Medi: Okay. .. [1:03:40] CHAT Amal: 5atibti btekrah enno ana ma anbese6 biel-3azoome (all 1041 turns, in order)
coverage_note: Lesson is a drill on the n-verbs (banze3ej / banbese6 / bankeser): most Medi Arabic is one-line answers to Amal's English prompts, so most rows are grammar on verb form. Long English-only stretches: 10:06-13:05 (homework talk, aslan), 21:01-22:06 (repetition talk), 27:40-28:10 (Meet dropout), 33:01-33:52 (the A-sound rule talk), 46:06-47:12, 49:06-50:21, 58:25-58:48, 1:01:28-1:02:31. Latin-letter Arabic from the engine (read as Arabic): 13:01 'ana mazuruj' = ana maz3ooj; 14:34 'en-enkis-enkistri' = enkasarti; 16:10 'Wahta' = wa7de; 16:38 'El Sadeeki' = el-sadeeqi; 19:03 'n-nitlab' = nel3ab; 19:48 'matze'ejni' = ma tez3ejni; 22:17 'el yam yam el' = el-yoam yoam el-; 37:52 'bienzaju' = byenze3ju; 40:20 'be wa'atik' = bi wa2tek; 41:22 'basatik' = basattek; 42:06 'Basatu' = basa6tu; 42:16 'Ajitu' = ajeetu; 50:35 'Bitenbasti' = btenbes6i; 52:45 'lissa'. Engine confusion: Amal's e5taret (I chose) is written اشتريت at 02:31, 03:09, 03:18 (her chat 'ana e5taret adall fi baiti' settles it); 01:14 بشتري is what she HEARD him say ('I thought you said اليوم اشتريت بيتي') so it is his, not the engine. 04:12 Amal بيعطوني = her chat bey2aat3uni (they interrupt me). 24:44 engine 'من شاف' = his attempt at naashef (Amal recast الجو ناشف). 28:22 Amal 'أزعجني' = za3ajni (her chat huwwe za3ajni), a confirmation not a fix. 59:29 Amal 'نبسِته' = nbasse6o said with the vowel, same verb he said. Not written as rows (S4 pronunciation): 05:17-05:22 هدرتها for حضرتها (ه for ح), 19:03 nitlab for nel3ab, 53:16 انبسينا missing ط (Amal 'you missed a letter'), 43:38 بي قهوتك for بقهوتك, 16:10 Wahta. Self-fixes before Amal (GR-22, not rows): 01:30 بشتري -> اشتغلت/بشتغل (but Amal had already reacted, see row 0914-1), 02:42 خل-- خلاص, 11:27 هون -> هلق, 13:53 ma tistamel -> ma tista3mli, 30:06 ما تنزعجش -> ما تنزعجي, 57:02 بسطك -> بسطت (her بسطتك at the same second). Not slips: 03:07/03:12 question about the shape of e5taret; 26:17 'No ال?' question; 36:15 'كل حدا or حدا?' question (she offered الكل); 1:01:58 'بكم مرة؟' = kaman marra (Medi 2026-10-02 rule); 05:42 'انبسطت كبير' read as engine for كتير (he said كتير at 05:38, her chat kteer). Echo-candidates file for this date: take_verb, laazem_noun, chat_latin, foreign_script all empty; the 4 candidates (118s 'uh,', 253s 'Mm.', 609s 'Ah, oops.') are real English fillers, no sound-alike Arabic. Chat lines used only for context (GR-19). Speaker labels look right throughout. Names: امريكا/أمريكا at 06:20-06:25 is a proper name, not counted.

rows.amal_said: اشتريت؟ ... Wow، مبروك. ... Oh، I thought you said اليوم اشتريت بيتي.
rows.why: He meant 'today I work at my house' (bashte8el) but said bashteri (I buy); Amal heard 'bought' and said mabrook, he asked 'did I say بشتري؟' and fixed to اشتغلت / بشتغل at 01:30-01:47 - his fix came after her reaction, so her echo is the signal; sheet: 'i work | ana bashteghel | أنا بشتغل' vs 'i buy | Ana bashteri | أنا بشتري'.
rows.english: Today I am working at my house.

rows.medi_said: uh، أشتري uh، في بي-- uh، في محلي. بس اليوم،
rows.chat: ta2reeban dayman bashte8el fi ma7alli bas el-yoam kaan 3indi ijtimaa3 u 5allas mit2a55er u ana e5taret adall fi baiti
rows.why: Second time the buy/work swap comes out ('I usually work in my shop'); her chat types bashte8el and she said nothing on voice - may be the engine repeating the 01:14 confusion, so best reading only (also no b- on it, B1, same uncertainty).
rows.english: I almost always work in my shop, but today...

rows.medi_said: uh، بـ-- اختارت بضل-- uh، اختارت أضل بيتي.
rows.chat: ... u ana e5taret adall fi baiti
rows.why: 'I chose to stay at my house' needs the preposition fi before baiti; he dropped it and Amal recast 'في بيتي', which he repeated.
rows.english: I chose to stay at my house.

rows.medi_said: في المحل. [ضحكة] في الـ، في البيت.
rows.chat: belbait. 3ashan lamma ana fi el-ma7al daayman muwazzafini bey2aat3uni
rows.why: Answering 'bet7eb el-shu8ul bil-bait aw bil-ma7al' he said fi el-bait and she recast bil-bait and typed belbait; may be only her nicer re-phrase (both prepositions exist), so low.

rows.medi_said: uh، interrupts me. I don't know how to say interrupt.
rows.chat: belbait. 3ashan lamma ana fi el-ma7al daayman muwazzafini bey2aat3uni
rows.why: Didn't-know: he said he does not know 'interrupt' and Amal supplied bey2aat3uni (engine wrote بيعطوني); not on her sheet, so tier 0 not tier 3.

rows.chat: 3utleti awal lu3be amrikiyye lalmawsem u ana 7deretha
rows.why: lu3be is feminine so the adjective is amrikiyye (her chat types it that way); he said the masculine amriki and she did not voice it.

rows.medi_said: Uh، do you guys use fas-فصل for the same season like a, a sports season?
rows.amal_said: I would say موسم for this type of season. ... للموسم.
rows.chat: 3utleti awal lu3be amrikiyye lalmawsem u ana 7deretha
rows.why: He asked whether fasel (sheet 'season | Fasel | فصل') covers a sports season and Amal supplied mawsem - a didn't-know, not a slip.

rows.medi_said: uh, uh، تـ uh ختارن اختارن اختارينا
rows.chat: ... kul el-zlaam ma3 s7aabhom e5tarna laa3ebeen u e7na 3melna feraqna
rows.why: Past 'we chose' is e5tarna; he built e5taarina with an invented -ina ending and Amal recast اخترنا (he then echoed اختارنا).
He reached for 'players / athletes' in English mid-sentence and Amal supplied laa3ebeen; the word is not on her sheet (grep player/athlete: nothing), so a didn't-know, tier 0.
Past 'we made' is 3melna; he said 3melina (same invented -ina ending as 06:45) and Amal recast.
He said 'our own teams' in English, Amal asked 'what is team?', he said no, she supplied faree2 / fera2 / fera2na; not on her sheet, so didn't-know tier 0.
Amal asked 'what's jama3 esem?'; he offered esmi and she supplied the broken plural asmaa2 which he repeated.

rows.amal_said: So how we will say it؟ It's different than English. We will say the nouns it's easy to remember them. ... So just سهل to remember them.
rows.why: He invented a plural adjective sahlaat to agree with asmaa2; Amal explained the phrase is 'el-asmaa2 sahel netzakkarhom' (sahel stays singular) and he repeated سهل.

rows.amal_said: So it's either you or we. 'Cause it's general. ... نتذكرهم.
rows.why: General 'easy to remember them' takes the we/you form; he used the I-form atzakkarhom and Amal prompted 'either you or we' until he said netzakkarhom.
'one of the homeworks' needs min (wa7ad min el-wajbaat); Amal only answered 'arba3a', best reading.
rows.english: I forgot one of the homeworks.

rows.amal_said: You broke. You broke the thing that you have to fix. Not you were broken.
rows.chat: ma testa3mli ay ishi 2abel ma tsall7i illi kasartih / shu kasarti
rows.why: For 'what you broke' he reached for the n-form enkasarti (got broken) and Amal said no, 'you broke, not you were broken'; he then said كسرتي.

rows.chat: wa7de min idain sadiqi enkasrat lamma kunna nel3ab ma3 ba3ad
rows.why: 'one of my friend's hands' needs the dual/plural idain; he said singular eed, Amal prompted 'Hands.' and he fixed إيدين.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. صديقي. No L 'cause there's ي. ... Because it's صديقي، my friend، I don't-- ما، ما بحتاج L.
rows.chat: wa7de min idain sadiqi enkasrat lamma kunna nel3ab ma3 ba3ad
rows.why: He put el- on sadeeqi in the idafa 'idain sadeeqi' (also at 16:29 إيد الصديقي); Amal named the rule: no el- when the word carries the -i owner ending.

rows.amal_said: One feminine. ... Yeah. بس، بس one broke. ... Mm. Feminine.
rows.why: The subject is wa7de (one hand, feminine singular) so the verb is enkasrat; he said the plural enkasaru, then masculine enkasar, Amal prompted 'one, feminine' twice until he said انكسرت.

rows.amal_said: We were playing. Where is the were? ... No، that would be played when we played. ... We took it with the used to.
rows.why: 'when we were playing' is kaan + present (kunna nel3ab); he used the plain past l3ebna and Amal prompted 'where is the were?' until he built كنّا نلعب.
Past 'we were' is kunna; he produced kunaina and Amal recast كنّا.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة أزرق و زرقا
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes bluze zar2a u short sakani u boat aswad
rows.why: bluze is feminine so the colour is zar2a; he said azra2, then 'u zar2a' as Amal said زرقا at the same second - reads as her recast he took up (his 'و' shows he was going on, not fixing), medium because the timing is tight.
rows.english: Today I'm wearing a blue blouse.

rows.medi_said: Hold on one second. الدّرجة حرارة؟
rows.why: Idafa: el- goes on the second word (darajet el-7arara), never the first; he said el-daraje 7arara and Amal recast, he repeated it right.

rows.medi_said: م-م-من شاف، من شاف؟ Try. (engine; his attempt at naashef)
rows.why: Explaining why 84F is not bad in California he groped for 'dry' (sheet 'dry | Naashef | ناشف'), the engine wrote من شاف, he said 'Try' and Amal supplied el-jaw naashef which he repeated; a word he could not get out, written as supplied-word tier 0.

rows.medi_said: المفضل لي-- or just مفضل لي. Right? No ال؟
rows.why: 'my favourite' is el-mufaddal 3indi; he used li and Amal recast 3indi, which he repeated (his question was about el-, her fix was the preposition).

For 'he made happy' the middle letter doubles (bassat); Amal echoed it long ('بسات') after his flat basat, then stopped the drill format - low because the engine cannot show the shadda and she did not say it was wrong.

rows.amal_said: شو بيزعجك؟ ... It's annoying you. مش...
rows.why: 'what is annoying you' is the make-form byez3ejek; he used the get-form byenze3ej (also at 31:50 بتنزعجي) and Amal recast; he said 'that's right, there's no N'.

'maybe we annoyed her' is za3ajna + -ha; he said tez3ejna (wrong person prefix, no object ending) and Amal recast; at 34:00 he tried تزعجنا again and she said 'it's neither, it's just za3ajna' - same moment.

rows.amal_said: You annoy me. ... Yes, you guys annoy me. مش be annoyed by.
rows.why: 'you guys annoy me' is the make-form btez3ejuni; he used the n- get-form and Amal said 'mish be annoyed by'; he fixed بتزعجوني.
'everyone gets annoyed by him' is the get-form byenze3ej; he offered the make-form baz3ej, Amal prompted 'gets annoyed' and he fixed بينزعج منه.
'enjoy your time' takes the -ak/-ek owner ending; he said bi-wa2ti (my time), Amal prompted 'your time' and he fixed bi wa2tik.
'did I make you happy' is past; he used the present babse6ak and Amal prompted 'maadi' until he moved to the past.
Second try at the same sentence dropped the I-ending -t (basatek = he made you happy); Amal recast basattek with the -t; a new slip after the tense fix, so a separate row.

rows.amal_said: بس. ... mm. ... I. I got happy.
rows.why: 'I got happy' is the n-form enbasa6et; he gave the make-form basa6et, Amal stopped him ('bas', 'mm') and he worked to انبسطت at 42:55.

rows.amal_said: Mm, mm. في كمان. في إشي. ناقص. ... بس قهوتك. What does it need? ... بقهوتك.
rows.why: enbasa6 takes bi before the thing enjoyed; he left it out, Amal said something is missing and prompted 'what does it need?' until he added بـ.
Amal asked rje3et? (are you back); 'I am back' is the past rje3et; he answered with the present barja3 and she said mm-mm and recast أنا رجعت.
'you get happy when you go out' is the n-form btenbes6i; he said btebse6i (you make happy) and Amal recast; he repeated Bitenbasti.
rows.english: You get happy when you go out.

rows.medi_said: من، أكثر من، أكثر من هذا.
rows.chat: intu laazem tenbes6u aktar min heik
rows.why: 'more than this' is aktar min heik (sheet 'like this / this way | Heik | هيك'); he used hada and Amal said heik, he asked 'heik or hada?' and she confirmed heik.

rows.medi_said: إنتو لازم ... انبسطوا ... أكثر من هيك.
rows.chat: intu laazem tenbes6u aktar min heik
rows.why: After laazem the verb is the bare you-plural present tenbes6u (her chat), not the command enbes6u; he said the command twice (51:53, 52:18) and Amal only typed the fix - no voiced signal.
rows.english: You guys should be happier than this.

rows.why: 'we didn't enjoy the party' takes enbasa6 + bi; he asked 'at the party or with the party?', went with ma3 el-7afle and Amal recast بالحفلة.
rows.english: We didn't enjoy the party much.

rows.why: Same fixed preposition: enbasa6 bi; he dropped bi before mashaweerek and Amal said 'be' (her chat bimashaweerek); he groaned 'oh my God'.
rows.english: He enjoys your outings a lot.

rows.amal_said: Did she make you happy؟ ... did.
rows.why: 'did she make you happy' is the past make-form bassatek; he gave the present get-form btenbese6, Amal re-asked the English and said 'did' until he built بسطت / بسطتك.
The sentence is about 'she' (heyye in her chat) and he said huwwe when repeating her fix; Amal let it pass - could be the engine, low.
'the gathering' needs el- (her chat biel-3azoome); he said bi-3azoome here and again at 1:01:16 before fixing himself to العزومة at 1:01:25; Amal only said mm-hmm / sa7.
Answering her بشوفك (see you) he dropped the object ending -ek; she had already said bye, no signal.
